restoration_note: The teaching describes two faces (ⲡⲣⲟⲥⲱⲡⲟⲛ) appearing from the inmost (face = inmost turned outward) in the higher reaches of the rational: the face of love (ⲁⲅⲁⲡⲏ, characterized as beauty-with-longing) and the face of love-of-strife (ⲙⲛⲧⲭⲁⲓ̈ⲙ̄ⲗⲁⲍ, the self's contention). The higher powers of heaven refine (ⲥⲱⲧϥ̄) the second face upward (ⲁⲍⲣⲏⲓ̈) so that what is claimed is laid off and only the face of love remains. All ten gaps are short, morphologically constrained, or already supplied by clear formulas: completion of ⲡⲣⲟⲥⲱⲡⲟⲛ across line breaks, the numeral ⲥⲛⲉⲩ ('two'), ⲧⲍⲣⲧⲉ ('the fear'), ⲉⲧⲭⲱⲃⲉ ('that is weak'), ⲡⲉⲓⲛⲉ ('likeness'), and ⲛ̄ⲍⲏⲧⲟⲩ ('from them'). The editor's proposals were confirmed throughout.

coptic_restorations.basis: Completes ⲡⲣⲟⲥⲱⲡⲟⲛ ('face') broken across the line; the form is fixed and the next segment continues with ⲍⲙ̄ ⲡⲡⲣⲟⲥⲱⲡⲟⲛ.

The reading enumerates two distinct faces (love and fear/strife); the cardinal ⲥⲛⲉⲩ is the natural opener for the doublet 'two: in the face of agape and the face of fear', paralleled later in §4541 ⲡⲉⲓⲛⲉ ⲅⲁⲣ ⲥⲛⲉⲩ.
Completes ⲡⲣⲟⲥⲱⲡⲟⲛ + relational ⲛ̄ ('face of'); the following segment opens with ⲧⲍⲣ̄ⲧⲉ, so the construction is ⲡⲣⲟⲥⲱⲡⲟⲛ ⲛ̄ⲧⲍⲣⲧⲉ 'face of the fear'.
Feminine definite article completing ⲧⲍⲣ̄ⲧⲉ ('the fear'), the second pole opposite ⲧⲁⲅⲁⲡⲏ in the two-faces enumeration.
Completes ⲥⲛⲉⲩ after ⲡⲓⲡⲣⲟⲥⲱⲡⲟⲛ; 'these two faces' matches §4541's ⲥⲛⲉⲩ ⲡⲡⲣⲟⲥⲱⲡⲟⲛ formula.
Completes the qualitative ⲉⲧⲭⲱⲃⲉ ('which is weak/small'); fits the soul of the powers of heaven described as still in the contest of refinement.
Single supralineated stroke completing ⲡⲉⲓⲛⲉ ('likeness'); the following ⲥⲛⲉⲩ ⲡⲡⲣⲟⲥⲱⲡⲟⲛ confirms 'two likenesses'.
Completes ⲡⲣⲟⲥⲱⲡⲟⲛ ⲛ̄- ('face of') broken across §4542 ⲡⲧⲕⲉⲡⲣⲟⲥⲱ-; the construction is 'the other face of the love-of-strife'.

Lycopolitan ⲛ̄ⲁⲍⲣⲏⲓ̈ (= Sah. ⲉϩⲣⲁⲓ̈) 'upward'; the verb ⲥⲱⲧϥ̄ 'refine/choose out' takes the upward-direction adverb in the regenerative sense — the powers refine the strife-face upward, sorting it toward the face of love.
Completes Lyc. ⲛ̄ⲍⲏⲧⲟⲩ (= Sah. ⲛ̄ϩⲏⲧⲟⲩ) 'from them', subject-resumption clause for the powers of heaven who do the refining.

english_segments.core_english: in the heavens habitually reveal themselves out of this face —
{0}: in the face of the love (agape) and the face of
the fear. They reveal themselves out of these {1} faces
of the powers of heaven that are in the heavens, on account of their soul that is {2}
in the All. For in likeness there are two: the face of A-
ce of the love-of-strife that is in them, which they habitually refine {3}

english_restorations.basis: Renders ⲥⲛⲉⲩ, the cardinal opening the two-faces enumeration of love and fear.
Renders ⲥⲛⲉⲩ qualifying ⲡⲓⲡⲣⲟⲥⲱⲡⲟⲛ — 'these two faces' that the powers reveal.
ⲉⲧⲭⲱⲃⲉ qualitative of ϣⲱⲃⲉ ('be weak/small'); 'weak' fits the soul still in refinement, where the strife-face has not yet been laid off.
Renders ⲁⲍⲣⲏⲓ̈ 'upward'; the directional adverb required by ⲥⲱⲧϥ̄ in regenerative use, where the powers refine the strife-face upward toward the face of love.
Renders ⲛ̄ⲍⲏⲧⲟⲩ 'from them' (the souls in whom the strife resides), with the dash continuing the refining action and introducing the subject 'the powers of heaven'.
